skill.name: meeting-insights-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes meeting transcripts and recordings to uncover behavioral patterns, communication insights, and actionable feedback. Identifies when you avoid conflict, use filler words, dominate conversations, or miss opportunities to listen. Perfect for professionals seeking to improve their communication and leadership skills.
skill.summary: Analyze meeting transcripts to identify communication patterns and coaching opportunities.

content.value_statement: Meeting transcripts contain useful signals, but reviewing them manually takes time. This skill turns transcripts into focused communication feedback with examples and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews transcript files for speaker labels, timestamps, meeting dates, and user identity cues.
Identifies patterns such as conflict avoidance, interruptions, filler words, and active listening.
Calculates communication metrics including speaking ratio, questions asked, and interruption counts.
Provides timestamped examples that explain what happened, why it matters, and how to improve.
Compares meetings over time to show changes in facilitation, listening, and directness.
Creates summaries, growth opportunities, and concrete next steps for communication development.
limitations: Analysis quality depends on accurate transcripts, clear speaker labels, and useful timestamps.
The skill cannot evaluate tone, body language, or audio that is missing from the transcript.
It may need the user to confirm names, roles, date ranges, or the behavior to review.
It does not replace human coaching, HR review, legal advice, or clinical assessment.

use_cases.title: Improve Leadership Communication
use_cases.description: Review recurring meetings to find patterns in directness, listening, facilitation, and decision making.

use_cases.title: Prepare Performance Review Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect concrete meeting examples that show communication strengths, growth areas, and behavior changes over time.

use_cases.title: Coach Meeting Facilitation
use_cases.description: Analyze team meetings to understand speaking balance, inclusion, interruptions, and follow-up clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one behavior across available transcripts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the meeting transcripts in this folder. Tell me when I used filler words and show the clearest examples.

prompt_templates.title: Review Communication Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of recurring leadership behaviors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my meetings from the past month. Identify my main communication patterns, strengths, and growth opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Meeting Sets
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across time periods or teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my Q1 and Q2 meeting transcripts. Show whether my listening, interruptions, and question quality improved.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Coaching Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced synthesis for a focused development plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these transcripts for conflict avoidance, speaking ratio, facilitation quality, and action item clarity. Create a prioritized coaching plan.

output_examples.input: Analyze my team meetings and tell me whether I dominate the conversation.
output_examples.output: The report highlights speaking percentage, turn length, missed openings for others, and examples where shorter framing would improve participation.

output_examples.input: Find moments where I avoided giving direct feedback.
output_examples.output: The output lists specific meetings and timestamps, explains the indirect language, and suggests clearer phrasing for each moment.

output_examples.input: Compare my listening skills between two folders of transcripts.
output_examples.output: The comparison summarizes changes in clarifying questions, interruptions, paraphrasing, and examples of stronger active listening.

best_practices: Use consistent file names with dates so the analysis can compare meetings over time.
Ask about one or two behaviors when you need deep evidence and practical advice.
Review sensitive transcript content before sharing outputs outside your organization.
anti_patterns: Do not use transcripts without permission from meeting participants or your organization.
Do not treat transcript analysis as objective truth when speaker labels or timestamps are unreliable.
Do not request broad feedback without defining the role, meeting type, and target behavior.

faq.question: What file types can this skill review?
faq.answer: It is designed for meeting transcript files such as text, markdown, VTT, SRT, and exported document text.

faq.question: Does it analyze audio directly?
faq.answer: The instructions focus on transcript analysis. Audio quality, tone, and pauses are only available if they appear in the transcript.

faq.question: Can it compare my progress over time?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare transcript sets by date range and summarize changes in communication patterns.

faq.question: Will it identify my speaking ratio?
faq.answer: Yes, when transcripts include speaker labels and enough structure to estimate speaking time or turn counts.

faq.question: Is this suitable for sensitive meetings?
faq.answer: Use caution. Keep transcripts local when possible and remove confidential information before sharing reports.

faq.question: Does it provide coaching recommendations?
faq.answer: Yes. It links observed patterns to practical next steps and alternative phrasing.
